text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages across ten settings, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, the Kelemba Water Trust completed 14 new boreholes across the Ndoro and Sasenga wards, bringing safe water within 500 metres of roughly 6,200 residents. Household latrine coverage rose from 38% to 61% over the twelve months, largely because trained artisans sold concrete slabs at cost. Water committees collected user fees in nine of the fourteen villages, and those funds paid for two pump repairs without outside help. However, the project did not meet its target for school handwashing stations, as only five of the planned eight were installed before the rains closed access roads. We have not yet seen a measurable fall in reported diarrhoea cases at Sasenga clinic, and we will review the data again in March 2024.

variants.added_negation: Water committees collected user fees in nine of the fourteen villages, and those funds never paid for two pump repairs without outside help.
variants.removed_negation: However, the project did meet its target for school handwashing stations

variants.paraphrase: Fewer than two-thirds of the planned school handwashing stations went in, because seasonal rains cut off roads.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Halvane Camp case management service, conducted in October 2022, found that caseworkers had opened 1,140 protection files since the project began. Around 72% of surveyed clients said they understood how to reach their assigned caseworker, and most rated the service as respectful. Unaccompanied children were prioritised, with 86 placed in interim care arrangements within three days of registration. The evaluators noted, however, that referrals to legal aid were slow and that women did not always feel safe reporting violence at the main registration tent. Staff turnover was high: four of the eleven caseworkers left in the first year. No confidential interview room had been built by the time of the review, which the team identified as the most urgent gap.

passages.source_passage: Session 4 introduces volunteers to the Mbalusi District household visit routine. Each community health volunteer is responsible for about 45 households and should visit every home at least once a month. Begin the session by asking participants to name three danger signs in a newborn; most groups will name fever but not fast breathing. Explain that a child with a fever lasting more than two days must be referred to Kiboro health centre the same day. Volunteers should never give medicine that has not been supplied through the programme kit. Allow 90 minutes for the role plays, and remind trainers that in the 2021 cohort roughly one in five volunteers forgot to record referrals in the register.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 reporting year, Lantern Families Network placed 63 separated children with approved foster carers in the Orvale and Brisk Hill districts. Family tracing teams followed up 118 cases and reunited 41 children with parents or close relatives, compared with 29 the previous year. Every reunification was preceded by at least two home assessments, and no child was returned to a household where risks had not been addressed. Foster carers received a monthly allowance and attended quarterly peer support meetings. We were unable to recruit enough carers for adolescents, and seven older boys remained in the interim centre for longer than six months. The grant from your foundation covered 40% of tracing costs this year.

passages.source_passage: This module prepares volunteer facilitators to run the Tessara Farmer Field School season, which lasts 16 weeks from planting to harvest. Each school should have between 20 and 25 members who share one demonstration plot of about a quarter of an acre. Facilitators lead the weekly agro-ecosystem analysis, in which small groups observe plants, pests and soil moisture before drawing conclusions together. Do not tell farmers which practice is better; let them compare the plots and decide. In past seasons, plots using mulch and compost yielded 30% more maize than the conventional plot, but facilitators should not promise this result. Record attendance every week, because schools with fewer than twelve active members by week eight rarely complete the season.

passages.source_passage: Quarter 3 monitoring at the Ravelstone Vocational Training Centre covered July to September 2024. Of the 210 young people enrolled, 174 attended at least 80% of sessions, and 52 completed the six-month tailoring, welding or solar installation courses during the quarter. Tracer calls reached 39 of the 52 graduates, and 23 reported paid work or self-employment within eight weeks. Female enrolment in welding remained low, with only three women in a class of thirty. The centre's toolkits for graduates weren't delivered on time, so most solar trainees left without the starter equipment promised at intake. Employer partners in Ravelstone town hired eleven apprentices, but no new partnerships were signed this quarter.

passages.source_passage: This mid-term evaluation reviewed the Nirmala Health Collective's clinic-outreach project in Charbagh sub-district between January 2021 and June 2023. Facility births among enrolled women rose from 46% at baseline to 68%, and outreach workers completed 3,900 postnatal home visits. Evaluators found that mothers valued the visits within 48 hours of delivery, particularly for breastfeeding advice. However, the project has not reached the hill hamlets east of the river, where travel to the clinic still takes more than two hours. Kangaroo mother care was introduced in only one of the four clinics, and staff there had no dedicated space for it. The evaluation recommends extending outreach to the hill hamlets before the final year begins.

variants.paraphrase: Only a quarter of the clinics had started kangaroo mother care, and even there it lacked its own room.

passages.source_passage: Between April and December 2023, the Open Path Inclusion Project distributed 318 assistive devices in Tamsel Vale and Corran district, including 142 wheelchairs, 96 hearing aids and 80 sets of crutches. Follow-up visits three months after fitting found that 88% of wheelchair users were still using their chairs daily. Hearing aid uptake was weaker, as replacement batteries were not available in local shops. Accessibility audits were completed at 12 schools and five health posts; ramps were built at seven schools, but none of the health posts had been modified by the end of the period. Community volunteers trained families to carry out basic wheelchair repairs. The project did not record disaggregated data on women with disabilities, which limits analysis.

variants.reordered: Families trained community volunteers to carry out basic wheelchair repairs.
variants.paraphrase: Because the project failed to collect sex-disaggregated figures, it cannot properly analyse outcomes for disabled women.

passages.source_passage: Since 2019, the Quiet Harbour Counselling Service has offered free, lay-led psychosocial support in the coastal town of Merrowby and its surrounding fishing villages. Demand has grown steadily: the service received 640 referrals in 2023, almost double the 330 it handled in 2020. A local survey found that one in four adults reported symptoms of persistent distress after the 2022 storm surge. There is no psychiatrist based in the district, and the nearest specialist clinic is 90 kilometres away. Our nine trained lay counsellors deliver a five-session problem-solving model, and clients who complete it report lower distress scores on average. Waiting times, however, now exceed six weeks, and many people do not return once they have been placed on the list.

passages.source_passage: The semi-arid plains of Kordessa County have recorded below-average rainfall in four of the last six years, and the 2022 long rains failed almost entirely. Most of the county's 28,000 farming households still plant a single local maize variety that does not tolerate dry spells longer than ten days. Field trials run by the Dunmere Agricultural Station showed that sorghum and drought-tolerant cowpea produced harvests even when rainfall fell 35% below normal. Yet seed of these varieties is not sold by any agro-dealer in the county, and extension officers cover areas of more than 400 square kilometres each. This project will establish community seed banks in 15 villages and train lead farmers to multiply and distribute improved seed.
